newsitem.title: USA: Doctors warn against taking online health advice.
newsitem.headline: Doctors warn against taking online health advice.

text.p: Health and medical information found on the Internet is more akin to cocktail party chat than sound advice, the American Medical Association warned consumers on Tuesday.

If anything there is too much information available in cyberspace, "vast chunks of it incomplete, misleading or inaccurate ... novices and savvy Internet users alike can have trouble distinguishing the wheat from the chaff, the useful from the harmful," the group said.

"When it comes to medical information, the Internet too often resembles a cocktail conversation rather than a tool for effective health care and decision making," it said in an editorial published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association.

The doctors' group suggested that standards be set for Internet medical data that would include clear identification and relevant credentials for authors and contributors, references for all content and a disclosure of web site ownership and any commercial funding.
